# Bender's Bar & Grill

> Punk and metal bar and grill on South Van Ness in San Francisco. Pool tables, pinball, jukebox and food. Rated 4.6 from 864 Google reviews.

- Type: Bar & Grill
- Address: 806 S Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94110, USA

## About
Bender's is like your parent's basement, and they're always out of town. It was started by drinkers that love to serve drinks to drinkers, and we ain't slowin down.
Shoot pool, play some pinball, put something loud on the jukebox. The kitchen keeps the grill side of the name honest, and Sunday is pizza night.
We're rated 4.6 on Google from 864 reviews. Bring your ID, it's an adults-only spot.

## Services
- Drinks: A full bar, poured by drinkers who love serving drinks to drinkers.
- A Lemmy: One reviewer's tip: don't leave without asking for a Lemmy.
- Food: There's a real kitchen here. One reviewer was happy to find pool tables, vibes and food all in one spot.
- Vegetarian selection: One reviewer called out the great vegetarian selection.
- Pizza: The kitchen does a pizza night once a week.
- Pool tables and pinball: Rack 'em up or grab a pinball machine while the jukebox plays.
- Photobooth: One reviewer pointed out the photobooth, so grab your crew and squeeze in.

## FAQ
Q: Will I get carded at the door?
A: Yes, bring your ID. One reviewer said the doorman checked his ID along with everyone else in his group.

Q: Where are you?
A: 806 S. Van Ness Ave in San Francisco, near the Mission.

Q: Do your hours change?
A: They can. Hours are subject to change, so check with us before you head over.

- "Just went with my adult children to play pool. Great atmosphere and friendly people. Only thing that sucked was the doorman who asked for my ID after checking my 23,26 year old kids. I’m 62. “Why?” I asked. “To make sure you are a real human being” he joked but he was serious and really wanted to see my ID suggesting that I “respect” him etc. No. If you respect me you don’t demand an ID from someone clearly of legal age. There was no possible legitimate reason for this crap. That started the visit on a bummer note but after ten minutes I wrote him off and we had a good time." (mark p, 4/5)
